title: The Sharp Safehouse
premise: Bram Halloran, a compliance investigator who has spent years laundering his conscience by following rules, is approached by a woman named Ilse who claims he saved her life in Prague—a favor he has no memory of performing. As Ilse pulls him into her orbit, Bram discovers a ledger of payments routed through the very banks he polices, implicating officials in three governments, and learns his forgotten act of kindness was actually a transaction he was drugged into facilitating. Hunted by an assassin named Voss who erases loose ends, Bram and Ilse race to move the evidence to a journalist before a financial summit grants the conspirators immunity. In the end, Bram must choose between destroying the ledger to save Ilse's life or publishing it and losing the last of his clean reputation; he splits the evidence, publishes half, and walks away a man who can no longer pretend the rules ever protected anyone.
about_author: Felix Blackwood is the pen name of a former financial auditor who spent a decade inside compliance departments before trading spreadsheets for fiction. He writes thrillers about ordinary professionals trapped in extraordinary moral arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Was
chapters.summary: Bram Halloran, POV. A meticulous day of flagging suspicious transactions ends with a stranger, Ilse, buying him a drink and thanking him for Prague—a city he can't recall visiting. Her parting gift is a bank key with his own handwriting on the tag. The beat is quiet dread: his tidy world has a crack in it.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. He investigates himself, finding a two-day gap in his records three years ago and a Prague hotel charge he can't explain. His firm's new director, Aldous Renner, smooths it over too easily. The beat is paranoia taking root beneath professional routine.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. She watches Bram from a distance, recalling the night in Prague when he unknowingly moved money for a syndicate that killed her sister. She needs his access and his testimony. The beat is calculated sympathy—her kindness toward him is a debt-collection strategy.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. The bank key opens a locker containing a ledger of payments linking Renner's firm to officials in three governments. Photographing it, he notices a gray sedan that's been outside his flat too long. The beat is the thrill of discovery curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: The assassin Voss, POV. A cold, professional chapter as he reviews his contract: retrieve the ledger, erase its courier. He notes Bram's habits with unsettling tenderness, the way he studies anything he intends to destroy. The beat is menace without violence.

chapters.title: Rewritten Rules
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. He reports the ledger internally and watches Renner bury it within hours, then finds his own security clearance suspended. The institution he served is the crime. The beat is betrayal—the rules were never walls, just paint.

chapters.title: Prague, Three Years Gone
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Chasing his memory gap, he finds his old passport with a Czech stamp and a fragment of memory: a hotel bar, a woman's laugh, a bitter taste in his glass. He was drugged and used as an unwitting courier. The beat is grief for his own naivety.

chapters.title: The Safehouse
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. She stashes Bram in a decommissioned bank vault—'the sharp safehouse'—her old syndicate's fallback. Their uneasy alliance forms over her confession of manipulation. The beat is two liars negotiating the first honest terms either has offered.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. He maps the ledger's beneficiaries: a British treasury aide, a German regulator, a Swiss prosecutor. Each is attending next month's Geneva financial summit, where a new secrecy accord will grant them retroactive immunity. The clock starts. The beat is vertigo at the scale of it.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. She contacts Mara Okafor, an exiled investigative journalist in Lisbon, and arranges a handoff—then discovers Voss has found Mara first and is watching her. The beat is hope complicated by the cost of every ally.

chapters.title: A Man Who Followed Rules
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Voss corners Bram alone and offers a trade: the ledger for his life and Ilse's. Bram stalls, lying for the first time in his career, and is shocked by how easily it comes. The beat is corruption's first taste—sweet, terrifying.

chapters.title: Renner's Offer
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Renner summons him, revealing he knows about the safehouse, and offers Bram a partnership: help bury the ledger, inherit a directorship. He frames it as the system working as designed. The beat is temptation wearing a mentor's face.

chapters.title: What Ilse Buried
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. Bram finds her hidden file on the syndicate and learns she was the one who drugged him in Prague—her sister's killers forced her. Her guilt explains her devotion. The beat is fury collapsing into shared complicity; both were used by the same machine.

chapters.title: The Vault Job
chapters.summary: Bram and Ilse, alternating POV. They return to his firm after hours to copy the ledger's authentication codes, executing a tense infiltration that nearly fails when Voss arrives early. They escape through a service corridor. The beat is adrenaline and the discovery that they trust each other now.

chapters.title: Lisbon
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. The handoff to Mara Okafor goes wrong; Voss kills her fixer, and Mara, spooked, demands the full story before accepting anything. Bram tells her everything, including his own crime. The beat is confession as liberation—naming his guilt out loud.

chapters.title: The Summit Approaches
chapters.summary: Ilse, POV. With days left, they learn Renner has accelerated the accord's signing. Voss captures Mara, forcing a choice: trade the ledger's codes for her life. The beat is the noose tightening; every path now runs through sacrifice.

chapters.title: Geneva
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Undercover at the summit among the very officials he's exposing, Bram plants a decoy ledger while Mara's dead-man's-switch release is armed. Renner, smiling, hands him a glass of champagne—the same bitter taste as Prague. The beat is history threatening to repeat itself.

chapters.title: The Trade
chapters.summary: Ilse and Bram, alternating POV. The exchange for Mara happens in an old customs house. Ilse offers herself in Bram's place; Voss, honoring some private code, accepts the codes instead—but they're forged, and he knows it. The beat is a standoff suspended on mutual recognition: hunter and hunted are the same kind of survivor.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Voss, POV. A revelation chapter: Voss was the syndicate's first courier, erased from records the way he erases others. He decides the ledger deserves to live—not from morality, but from grievance. The beat is the assassin's cold heart cracking open.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Clean
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. Climax. Renner confronts Bram in the summit's vault level; Voss arrives, and in the chaos Renner is exposed by the live release of the ledger to forty newsrooms. Renner falls; Voss walks away, sparing Bram with a look that says 'we're even.' The beat is catharsis with blood on it.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Bram, POV. The accord collapses, investigations begin, and Bram testifies—destroying his career to salvage his conscience. Ilse, cleared but exiled, chooses to leave. The beat is the price of survival made concrete: truth costs everything it touches.

chapters.title: The Sharp Edge of Ordinary
chapters.summary: Bram, POV, one year later. Working a small-town fraud desk, Bram receives a postcard from Prague with no message—Ilse's sign of life. He keeps the ledger's final page, the one naming him, as a reminder. The beat is quiet resolution: memory is the only safehouse, and he finally lives in it honestly.
